item.text: {"0":"Across all four datasets, change only masked-target loss weighting: give targets at the final sequence position weight 2 and other masked targets weight 1, normalizing by the total target weight. Keep full-vocabulary cross-entropy and temperature 0.8. This may better align training with appended-mask prediction while retaining bidirectional context learning. Preserve masking, sampling, architecture, optimizer and inference.","1":"Across all four datasets, multiply each Transformer feed-forward residual contribution by 0.5, leaving attention residuals unchanged. This may preserve contextual attention signals while limiting feed-forward distortion on short histories, providing a smaller architectural intervention than the regressed GEGLU replacement. Retain existing GELU sublayers, dimensions, normalization, embeddings, readout, loss and optimizer; use identical residual scaling in training and prediction.","2":"Across all four datasets, jointly set MAXLEN=64, batch size=256 and learning rate=1e-3, retaining dropout=0.1. Most observed histories fit within 64 positions; reducing padded attention computation makes room for a larger batch, while the moderate learning-rate increase compensates for its lower gradient noise. Preserve BERT4Rec modules, representation, loss, optimizer type, readout, seed 42, 200 batches per epoch and the 200-epoch cap; save matching predictor metadata.","3":"Across all four datasets, change only the tied normalized item-embedding radius multiplier from 0.75 to 0.74. The regressions at 0.70 and 0.775 motivate a smaller local probe around the incumbent rather than assuming a monotonic benefit. Preserve width 64, input/output tying, frequency modulation, topology, scoring, history, loss temperature and optimizer. Apply the identical effective-weight definition during training and prediction."}
